builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LEDGER: Auditable Agent Memory Under Change
summary: The method replaces full-history replay, raw-transcript retrieval, and opaque memory stores like Mem0 with a structured ledger where explicit rules—not the model—decide currency, source precedence, and deletion, plus an episodic search fallback scrubbed on deletion requests. The cost is a memory-writing pipeline (an LLM pass to propose facts), rule maintenance, and a search component, though inference context shrinks to roughly 1% of full replay. What can fail: the main benchmark is synthetic and self-built, LongMemEval gains are within confidence intervals, and correctness depends on the fact-extraction model and rule coverage of the specific workload.
rationale: The rule-based memory layer is feasible on one GPU or via APIs and directly addresses compliance-relevant deletion and auditability, but the evidence base is a self-constructed synthetic benchmark with statistically inconclusive public-benchmark results, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Rule-governed auditable agent memory with episodic fallback

LEDGER+EP fallback answers 94.3%/91.1% correctly on development/held-out coding seeds versus 82.1%/83.3% for full replay; on LongMemEval it matches full replay accuracy (74.8%) using 1% of its context.
